changes.text: 8日，格兰特跟着在李军后方的波托马克军行进，正犯着重头痛，在路边一处离大部队有一段距离的农舍过夜，把脚泡进热水和芥末，手腕和后颈贴上芥末膏，指望天亮就能好。李来信提议会面。格兰特的回信很干脆：他无权谈和，这样的会面不可能有好结果；和平的条件众所周知，南方只要放下武器，就能让和平早点到来，救下成千上万条人命和数以亿计尚未被毁的财产。

On the 8th Grant followed the Army of the Potomac, which was in rear of Lee, in the grip of a sick headache. He spent the night at a farmhouse on the road, some distance behind the main body of the army, bathing his feet in hot water and mustard and putting mustard plasters on his wrists and the back of his neck, hoping that by morning he would be cured. A letter from Lee proposed a meeting. Grant's answer was brisk. He had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and the proposed meeting could lead to no good. The terms on which peace could be had, he wrote, were well understood: let the South lay down its arms, and the most desirable event would come sooner, sparing thousands of lives and hundreds of millions of property not yet destroyed.

格兰特收到信时还在头痛，一看到信的内容就好了。他回信说，因为他已从里士满—林奇堡路转到法姆维尔—林奇堡路，上午11点50分才拿到信；此刻在沃克教堂以西约四英里，正向前赶去会面，请对方在这条路上通知会面地点。赶到谢里登那里时，那里的人情绪激动，认定这是南军脱身的诡计：他们相信约翰斯顿正从北卡罗来纳北上，李要去会合；只要格兰特点头，五分钟内就能把对方打垮。格兰特不怀疑李的诚意，不久便被领到李所在之处。

The officer found Grant still suffering with the sick headache; in Grant's own telling, "the instant I saw the contents of the note I was cured." He wrote back at once. His note had reached him only at 11:50 a.m., he explained, because he had passed from the Richmond and Lynchburg road to the Farmville and Lynchburg road; he was at that moment about four miles west of Walker's Church and would push forward to the front for the meeting; a message left on this road naming the place would reach him. When he rode up to Sheridan's position, the men there were very much excited. They were convinced the whole thing was a ruse to let the Confederates get away. Johnston, they believed, was marching up from North Carolina and Lee moving to join him, and they would whip the rebels where they stood in five minutes if only Grant would let them go in. Grant had no doubt of Lee's good faith, and was soon conducted to where he was.
The Meeting at the McLean House
一种解释是，佩刀和私马这两条的意义不在让步大小，而在它们出现的位置：不是谈判桌上换来的，是起草人自己写进去的。作者推断，写进条文的成本几乎为零——武器、火炮和公物反正都要上交；收益则是让名册、宣誓这些真正要执行的条款少遇阻力。对方读到这一段时的反应，据格兰特说，是这会对他的军队有良好影响。

One reading of the side-arms and private horses is that what matters is not the size of the concession but where it appears: it was not traded for at the negotiating table but written in by the drafter himself. The inference here is that the cost was close to nil — arms, artillery and public property had to be surrendered anyway — while the payoff was less resistance to the clauses that actually had to be carried out, the rolls and the paroles. When Lee read that passage, Grant recorded, he remarked that this would have a happy effect upon his army.
至于叫停鸣炮，一种解释是，受降条件里最后一项从不写在纸上：胜利方当天说的第一句话。作者提出的替代做法是，把收缴佩刀之类的要求当作威慑保留下来，让对方记住谁说了算；代价可能是执行阶段无人配合，因为真正要办的事——交名册、办宣誓、放人回乡——都得靠对方的人去做。

As for halting the salute, one reading is that the last clause of any surrender is never set on paper: it is the first thing the winning side says that day. The alternative the writer offers is to keep demands such as handing over side-arms on the books as a reminder of who is in charge. The cost might be an unwillingness to cooperate in the carrying out, because the things that genuinely have to be done — delivering the rolls, taking the paroles, sending the men home — depend on the other side's people doing them.
本文唯一的史源是格兰特本人的回忆录，标注年份为1885–86年，成书于事件之后。文中对话都是他的转述，未必逐字；米德、谢里登、李的说法也都经他一手记录。

The sole source for this article is Grant's own memoirs, dated 1885–86 and written after the events. Every conversation in them is his retelling and need not be verbatim, and the words of Meade, Sheridan and Lee all reach us through him alone.
全文只有一个史源，即格兰特本人的回忆记述。对话是他的转述，未必逐字；他明言不知李的心情；本文不替任何一方补写心理；马匹宽许只是口头指示，落实情况、名册与宣誓的逐项执行，原文均未交代；日期按原文写法，不补年份。

There is only one source for this piece: Grant's own account in his memoirs. The conversations are his retellings and need not be verbatim; he says expressly that he did not know Lee's feelings, and this piece does not supply psychology for either side; the allowance on horses and mules was verbal only, and neither its implementation nor the item-by-item execution of the rolls and paroles is reported; dates are kept in the original wording, with no year supplied.
李随即写信接受条件，说条款与格兰特8日来信中所提的实质相同，他将指定军官来办交接。在告辞之前，他说自己的军队状况很糟：缺粮，没有草料，士兵连日只吃炒玉米，需要请格兰特供应口粮和草料，大约两万五千人。格兰特说当然可以，让李派自己的军需官和军需主任到两三英里外的阿波马托克斯车站，从被截停的列车上取用所需。

Lee promptly wrote accepting the terms: being substantially the same as those expressed in Grant's letter of the 8th, they were accepted, and he would designate the proper officers to carry the stipulations into effect. Before taking his leave he added that his army was in a very bad condition for want of food, and without forage; his men had been living for days on parched corn exclusively, and he would have to ask Grant for rations and forage. Grant agreed at once and asked how many men needed rations; about twenty-five thousand, Lee answered. Grant authorized him to send his own commissary and quartermaster to Appomattox Station, two or three miles away, where out of the trains the Union had stopped they could have all the provisions wanted.

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上农舍离大部队有一段距离、和平条件众所周知两处；英文删去关于日期写法的插入语，中英现已对等。

evidence.quote: some distance in rear of the main body of the army
The terms upon which peace can be had are well understood

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上信迟到的原因（从里士满—林奇堡路转到法姆维尔—林奇堡路），句末补上不久被领到李所在之处；顺带把会面地点改为在这条路上通知，与英文一致。英文未改。

evidence.quote: in consequence of my having passed from the Richmond and Lynchburg road to the Farmville and Lynchburg road
pretty soon was conducted to where he was

dispositions.rationale: 证据中没有出现桌子，标题改为“麦克莱恩家的会面／The Meeting at the McLean House”。

evidence.quote: I found him at the house of a Mr. McLean, at Appomattox Court House

dispositions.rationale: 英文末句改为由李说出、格兰特转述，与中文一致；中文未改。

evidence.quote: he remarked, with some feeling, I thought, that this would have a happy effect upon his army

dispositions.rationale: 英文 The cost would be 改为 The cost might be，与中文“代价可能是”的推测语气一致。
删去“写于”和 some years after 的说法，改为“标注年份为1885–86年，成书于事件之后／dated 1885–86 and written after the events”，不再推断写作或出版时间，也不隐含事件年份。
主语改为“本文／this piece”，避免读成格兰特不写心理；格兰特确实写了自己的心情。

evidence.quote: but my own feelings, which had been quite jubilant on the receipt of his letter, were sad and depressed

dispositions.rationale: 英文中“certainly”“About twenty-five thousand”两处加引号的引语，与证据的大小写和标点不完全一致，检查器因此误判出非逐字引语。现改为不加引号的转述，内容不变；中文未改。

evidence.quote: and asked for how many men he wanted rations
